research_question: Why do people forget names even when they recognize a face?

sources.title: Strategies to resolve recall failures for proper names: New data
sources.reliability: Peer-reviewed research indexed by the U.S. National Library of Medicine
notes: Proper names are particularly vulnerable to retrieval failures; people often search semantic and contextual cues when a name will not come to mind.

sources.title: Rehabilitation of memory for people's names
sources.reliability: Peer-reviewed clinical research indexed by the U.S. National Library of Medicine
notes: Training strategies that make names more meaningful can support learning and retrieval in people with memory impairment.

sources.title: Age-Related Increases in Tip-of-the-tongue are Distinct from Decreases in Remembering Names
sources.reliability: Peer-reviewed research available through the U.S. National Library of Medicine
notes: Tip-of-the-tongue experiences and successful name recall are related but distinguishable processes; name retrieval depends on several brain systems.
